lba_qa.q: When you soak dry raisins (ona drakshi) in water overnight, they swell up. Which cellular process causes this and how?
lba_qa.a:
This is OSMOSIS.

Process:
- Inside the raisin, the concentration of solutes is high (less water)
- Outside, the plain water has more water
- Water moves from outside (high water) INTO the raisin through the cell membrane
- The raisin swells up ✅

Osmosis = movement of water across a semi-permeable membrane from high water concentration to low water concentration.

lba_qa.q: When you wash clothes for a long time, the skin on your fingertips shrinks and wrinkles. Explain this using osmosis.
lba_qa.a:
Soap/water solution outside the skin is a HYPERTONIC solution (more concentrated than the cells).

Process:
- Water moves OUT of the skin cells into the surrounding solution by osmosis
- The cells lose water and shrink
- This makes the fingertip skin wrinkle ✅

This is EXOSMOSIS — water leaving the cell when the outside solution is more concentrated.

lba_qa.q: A salted vegetable (like cucumber sprinkled with salt) releases water after some time. Why does the water come out?
lba_qa.a:
Salt outside the vegetable cells makes a HYPERTONIC (concentrated) solution.

Process:
- The cell contents have more water than the salty outside
- By osmosis, water moves OUT of the vegetable cells into the salt
- So water collects on the surface ✅

This is why salt is used to preserve pickles — it draws water out and prevents microbes from growing.

lba_qa.q: Mitochondria is called the 'powerhouse of the cell'. How does its structure help it perform this role?
lba_qa.a:
Mitochondria produce energy (ATP) for the cell through respiration.

How structure helps:
- It has a DOUBLE membrane
- The inner membrane is folded into CRISTAE
- These folds greatly INCREASE the surface area ✅
- More surface area = more space for energy-releasing reactions

So mitochondria release energy (ATP) efficiently — hence 'powerhouse of the cell'.

lba_qa.q: Lysosomes are called 'suicide bags' of the cell. Why do they get this name?
lba_qa.a:
Lysosomes contain strong DIGESTIVE ENZYMES.

Normal job:
- They break down old, worn-out cell parts and foreign material (cleaning)

Why 'suicide bags':
- If a cell is damaged or dying, the lysosomes BURST
- Their enzymes digest the cell's OWN parts and destroy the cell ✅

So because they can destroy their own cell, lysosomes are called suicide bags.

lba_qa.q: A plant cell has a cell wall but an animal cell does not. How does this help the plant?
lba_qa.a:
The CELL WALL is made of cellulose and lies outside the cell membrane.

How it helps plants:
1. Gives the cell a fixed SHAPE and rigidity
2. Provides mechanical STRENGTH and support to the plant ✅
3. Protects the cell from bursting when too much water enters
4. Helps the plant stand upright without bones

Animal cells have no cell wall, so they have flexible shapes and need a skeleton for support.
lba_qa.topic: Cell Wall - Plant vs Animal Cell

lba_qa.q: Why is the cell membrane called a 'selectively permeable' membrane, and why is this important?
lba_qa.a:
Selectively permeable = it allows ONLY certain substances to pass through, not everything.

Importance:
- It lets in useful substances (food, oxygen, water)
- It keeps out or removes harmful/waste substances
- It controls what enters and leaves the cell ✅

This keeps the inside of the cell stable (homeostasis). If it let everything in, the cell could be harmed.

lba_qa.q: Robert Hooke saw 'little boxes' under his microscope and named them cells. What was he actually looking at, and why is the microscope important here?
lba_qa.a:
Robert Hooke looked at a thin slice of CORK (dead plant tissue) under his microscope.

What he saw:
- Tiny box-like empty compartments
- He named them 'cells' (like small rooms) ✅

Why the microscope matters:
- Cells are far too small to see with the naked eye
- The microscope magnifies them so we can study their structure
- This discovery started the study of cells (cell biology)

lba_qa.q: The nucleus is called the 'control centre' or 'brain' of the cell. Justify this name.
lba_qa.a:
The nucleus controls all cell activities.

Reasons it is the control centre:
- It contains the genetic material DNA (chromosomes)
- DNA carries instructions for all cell functions
- It controls cell GROWTH, REPRODUCTION and METABOLISM ✅
- It directs which proteins the cell makes

Just like the brain controls the body, the nucleus controls the cell. So it is rightly called the control centre.

lba_qa.q: Differentiate between a prokaryotic cell and a eukaryotic cell with one example each.
lba_qa.a:
PROKARYOTIC CELL:
- Has NO true (membrane-bound) nucleus
- Genetic material lies free in the cytoplasm (nucleoid)
- No membrane-bound organelles
- Example: Bacteria ✅

EUKARYOTIC CELL:
- Has a TRUE membrane-bound nucleus
- Has membrane-bound organelles (mitochondria, ER, etc.)
- Example: Plant cell, Animal cell ✅

Main difference: presence (eukaryotic) or absence (prokaryotic) of a true nucleus.

lba_mcq.q: Dry grapes (raisins) placed in a bowl of water become plump and swollen after a few hours. Which process is responsible?
options: Diffusion of sugar out of grapes
lba_mcq.explanation: Water moves from the surrounding dilute solution into the raisin (which has concentrated contents) through the semi-permeable membrane by osmosis, making it swell.

lba_mcq.q: A gardener over-fertilises a plant with too much salt around the roots, and the plant wilts. Why does excess salt harm the plant?
options: Water leaves the root cells by osmosis (exosmosis)
Salt adds extra water to the cells
Salt makes the soil too cold
lba_mcq.explanation: Excess salt makes the soil solution hypertonic. Water moves OUT of the root cells by osmosis, so the plant loses water and wilts.

lba_mcq.q: A cell with many folded inner membranes (cristae) and a double membrane is found to release energy. Which organelle is it?
lba_mcq.explanation: Mitochondria have a double membrane with inner folds (cristae) that increase surface area for energy (ATP) production — the powerhouse of the cell.

lba_mcq.q: During an infection, certain organelles burst and digest the damaged cell completely. Which organelle behaves like a 'suicide bag'?
lba_mcq.explanation: Lysosomes contain digestive enzymes. When a cell is damaged, they burst and digest the cell's own contents, hence the name 'suicide bag'.

lba_mcq.q: A pickle (uppinakaayi) stays fresh for months because salt is added. How does salt prevent spoilage at the cell level?
options: Salt draws water out of microbe cells by osmosis, killing them
lba_mcq.explanation: The salty (hypertonic) environment draws water out of microbial cells by osmosis. Without water, microbes cannot survive, so the pickle is preserved.

lba_mcq.q: Which feature is found in a plant cell but NOT in an animal cell, giving the plant rigidity?
lba_mcq.explanation: The cell wall (made of cellulose) is present only in plant cells. It gives shape, rigidity and mechanical support. Animal cells lack a cell wall.

lba_mcq.q: Robert Hooke first observed cells in 1665. What material did he examine under his microscope?
lba_mcq.explanation: Robert Hooke observed a thin slice of cork and saw box-like compartments, which he named 'cells'. This marked the discovery of cells.

lba_mcq.q: A bacterial cell has its genetic material lying free in the cytoplasm with no surrounding membrane. What type of cell is it?
lba_mcq.explanation: A prokaryotic cell (like bacteria) has no true membrane-bound nucleus; the genetic material lies free in the cytoplasm (nucleoid region).

lba_mcq.q: The cell membrane allows oxygen and food in but keeps many other substances out. What is this property called?
lba_mcq.explanation: The cell membrane is selectively (semi) permeable — it permits only certain substances to pass, controlling what enters and leaves the cell.

lba_mcq.q: Ribosomes in a cell are mainly responsible for which function?
lba_mcq.explanation: Ribosomes are the site of protein synthesis — they assemble amino acids into proteins as directed by the genetic material.
